Hi Dylan,

Attached is MedCore's initial redline to Redwood's DPA (MedCore_DPA_redline_v1.docx). Key asks in this pass:

- Confirm which party will act as controller/processor for telemetry and support logs (MSA currently lists both in different places).
- We need a mapping of subprocessors and an explicit transfer-impact addendum for EEA -> US processing (SCCs are included but our privacy team would like transfer-specific language).

Sophie — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary.

We're happy to walk through the redline live. Quick responses to your three bullets so we can triage before a meeting:

- Roles: Redwood's standard position is processor for customer-provided content and controller for limited telemetry used for platform health. That said, we can adopt language that clarifies the split per data category (we'll propose explicit clauses).
- Subprocessors: we will provide the current Subprocessor list and an onboarding cadence. We'll also confirm whether any new partners impact EEA transfers.
- Order Form scope: Monica (cc'd) will confirm whether the product line items you flagged expand categories; if so we'll provide a trimmed Order Form or a cross‑reference clause to the DPA.

I'll attach our internal response notes and a marked-up DPA for your counsel to review. Suggest we set a 30-minute call Tuesday 2026-11-30 15:00 ET — does that work for your team?

Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCCs / transfer impact — counsel notes

Dylan / Sophie —

We reviewed MedCore's redline and Redwood's initial notes. A few high‑priority items from counsel:

1) Transfer mechanism: SCCs are fine as a baseline, but please add an explicit Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) reference or an express EEA->US addendum that lists safeguards and relevant subprocessors.
2) Role certainty: the MSA should include a short table (in the DPA or as an exhibit) enumerating data categories and whether Redwood acts as controller or processor for each. Avoid ambiguous "both parties" language.
3) Indemnity / breach notification: recommend a 48-hour initial notification window for security incidents plus a 30-day remediation plan submission.

I've attached a clean amendment showing suggested SCC language and a short exhibit that can slot into the Order Form for transfer-specific points. Please treat the attached as draft language (BakerLee_SCCs_amendment.docx).

If helpful, we can join the Tuesday call to walk legal points.

Regards,

Thomas Baker
Baker & Lee LLP (external counsel to MedCore)

Sophie — following up with the specific Order Form questions you raised. Inline below are the short answers and proposed edits.

> "Order Form does not broaden data categories beyond what is listed in the DPA"
- Confirmed: Product line item "Usage Analytics" referenced in the Order Form is limited to aggregated, non‑PII telemetry. We will remove a stray bullet that referenced "extended profiling" which caused the concern. See attached redline: OrderForm_changes_redlined.docx.

> "Confirm which party will act as controller/processor for telemetry and support logs"
- Proposed exhibit: "Data Categories & Roles" that maps Product Events = processor (Redwood), Support Logs = processor (Redwood), Customer User Data = controller (MedCore). This exhibit will be included as an Order Form annex.

Next steps (proposal):
- Monica to deliver cleaned Order Form and Redwood DPA with tracked changes by Monday 2026-11-29 EOD.
- Hannah to validate SCC/inventory impacts and confirm whether any subprocessors require processor-to-processor agreements.
- Dylan to coordinate the Tuesday 11/30 sync and invite MedCore legal + Baker & Lee.

Thanks —
Monica
